items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: Joe Oliver had, he had Louis Kepard on the guitar, Pop Foster on the bass, and Willie Foster on the violin.

ctx.x: What about Abadese? Did you ever go by Abadese? Down there, I figured it was on the anvil. Well, it had another name and I can't remember. Something like the, the Princeton Inn or the Princeton Club or something like that. No, Joe Oliver used to be there with Big Eye Louie and Ernest Rogers and Wooden Joe was in there playing clarinet. Yeah. You know the place. That was the Magnolia band. No, I think Richard M. Jones was there. Not the Magnolia. Not the band that was on Hunts and Nagels, but another one. This is…

Olavon and Wooden Joe. Yeah, well, no, he had a whole band. Oh yeah, he had a whole band? Joe Oliver had a whole band. Mm-hm. Celestane. Joe Oliver had, he had Louis Kepard on the guitar, Pop Foster on the bass, and Willie Foster on the violin. That was Pop Foster's brother. And, uh, that's the, uh, the famous clarin, uh, clarinet and saxophone, uh, hot dog.
Where did he die? The clarinet play, is that the one that went up north or stayed here?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: he played a little while, yeah. But he didn't play long. He ain't, he wasn't much of him.

ctx.x: That was the Magnolia band. Do you remember, uh, I think, uh, Louie Kepard tells me that he played in the Magnolia band too with Oliver for a while.
He played, he played, he played, he played, he played, he played a little while, yeah. But he didn't play long. He ain't, he wasn't much of him. He played a little while.
Uh huh. And you played guitar then, but that was before Louie Kepard then, you joined him.
